title: Compass and Horizon
premise: Coral Underhill has spent two decades flying cargo and gossip across a forgotten river country, keeping his past sealed as tightly as the chest the flood season coughs up from a drowned colonial outpost. When the chest's contents—a ledger, letters, and proof of a massacre the old empire buried—draw a rival expedition and government men into the interior, Coral must guide a ragtag crew of salvagers, a cartographer named Ines Vale, and the orphan girl he quietly raised to the site before the dry season strands them all. Along the way he must choose between the duty to keep the secret that protects the river's surviving families and the love growing between him and Ines, who is chasing the truth of her grandfather's disappearance there. The expedition returns home with the chest surrendered to the families themselves, Coral's secret spoken aloud at last, and a new life measured in years rather than miles.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge is the pen name of a former bush-strip radio operator who spent a decade in remote river settlements collecting the stories pilots tell only at altitude. She writes adventure novels where the landscape keeps the receipts and the maps are never quite finished.

chapters.title: Fuel, Weather, Gossip
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine medicine run establishes his world: the river, the strips, the rumor economy, and the orphan girl Wren he pretends isn't his responsibility. Emotional beat: competent solitude hiding a man who has stopped counting years.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Low water after the floods exposes the chest stamped with a dead nation's seal near a drowned outpost. He hauls it home intending to sell it unopened. Beat: curiosity wrestling with the instinct to stay invisible.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, alone at night. He breaks the seal: shipping ledgers, ration tallities, and letters hinting at a massacre the old empire erased from record. One letter names a family—Vale. Beat: dread; he recognizes the name.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She arrives on the mail flight hunting her grandfather's last survey, armed with half a map. Coral lies smoothly. Beat: instant, inconvenient attraction sharpened by deception.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The girl has seen the chest and asks Coral what he's hiding. He gives her a job instead of an answer. Beat: found-family friction; loyalty as a form of love.

chapters.title: Men from the Ministry
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Government surveyors arrive asking about salvage rights and a sealed file. Coral realizes the chest is a liability, not a treasure. Beat: the past knocking on a door he bolted twenty years ago.

chapters.title: The Salvage Crew
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Coral's POV. He assembles an expedition—mechanic Bo, diver Tomas, cook Ferro—officially to recover a wreck, unofficially to move the chest somewhere no one will look. Beat: reluctant leadership; found family forming around a lie.

chapters.title: Half a Map
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She corners Coral with her grandfather's half-map; the missing half matches terrain only Coral knows. She proposes partnership. Beat: two secrets circling each other like aircraft.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The dry season clock starts: the river drops, the strips soften, and the ministry men book passage on the same flight. Coral must leave before they do. Beat: ticking-clock tension begins.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The expedition travels by boat and foot; Ines and Coral trade guarded stories. Wren stows along despite his objections. Beat: warmth growing inside a lie of omission.

chapters.title: The First Wreck
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A decoy dive at a genuine wreck buys the crew time and nearly costs Tomas his life. Coral's cover story holds—barely. Beat: the cost of deception made physical.

chapters.title: Night Radio
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A storm grounds them; by firelight Ines reads her grandfather's letters aloud. Coral realizes her family's loss is stitched to his secret. Beat: intimacy through grief; the lie begins to hurt.

chapters.title: The Ministry Follows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The surveyors' boat shadows them upriver; Coral runs a night passage through rapids to lose them, wrecking the prop. Beat: adrenaline, and the crew learning their captain lies well.

chapters.title: Stranded at Sable Bend
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Repairs at an abandoned mission station; Wren finds children's graves from the outpost era and asks the question no one answers. Beat: the massacre's human scale arrives.

chapters.title: The Other Half
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cornered by Ines, Coral admits the map's other half exists—inside the chest. He shows her the ledger but not the letters naming her family. Beat: half-truths as a kindness that curdles.

chapters.title: Ines's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She agrees to continue, but on her terms: when they find the site, she reads everything. Coral, loving her now in earnest, agrees. Beat: love against duty, terms drawn.

chapters.title: Bo's Doubt
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The mechanic confronts Coral privately: he's flown with liars before, and liars get crews killed. Beat: the crew's trust becomes the story's true cargo.

chapters.title: The Drowned Outpost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the site at dead-low water: foundations, a bell, and evidence the outpost's people didn't evacuate—they were removed. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: What the Bell Says
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The mission bell bears her grandfather's foundry mark; his survey wasn't cartography—it was testimony. Beat: her quest and Coral's secret collide.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, alone with the chest. She reads the letters naming the Vales among the removed families—and Coral's own childhood name among the survivors' children. Beat: betrayal and revelation in one breath.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Water
chapters.summary: Ines and Coral, alternating POV. She demands to know why he hid that he was one of the outpost children smuggled out and renamed. Beat: the midpoint rupture; love against duty turns inward.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback woven into the present night. How a boy was flown out, renamed, and taught to keep moving. Beat: the reader finally holds the whole map of his heart.

chapters.title: The Surveyors Arrive
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, Wren's. The ministry boat arrives at the site; the lead surveyor reveals the file was never closed and the families were promised compensation never paid. Beat: the enemy becomes complicated.

chapters.title: Confiscation Order
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The chest is seized for 'archival review'; the crew is ordered downriver. Coral sees the truth being re-buried by paperwork. Beat: duty to the dead versus duty to the state.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The girl photographs the ledger pages on a salvaged camera and hides the film in the plane's tail. Beat: the next generation refuses the silence.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The crew flies out through a storm front with a failing engine and the ministry men aboard. Beat: white-knuckle survival; trust tested at altitude.

chapters.title: Forced Landing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A crash landing on a sandbar; no deaths, but the plane is crippled and the chest damaged, spilling letters across the sand. The surveyors see everything. Beat: the secret is out whether Coral wills it or not.

chapters.title: What the Families Are Owed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Stranded together, the surveyor's junior officer admits the ministry wants the file closed before centenary ceremonies. Ines proposes a different ending: give it to the families first. Beat: alliance forms across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Repair
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Three days rebuilding the engine from wrecks along the sandbar while the river drops further. Beat: found family working as one body; hope machined from scrap.

chapters.title: The Junior Officer's Decision
chapters.summary: Junior officer Reyes's POV. He must choose between his career and the ledger. He copies the manifest and lets the original 'fall' into the river. Beat: small courage changing the story's direction.

chapters.title: Flight Home
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The overloaded flight home through smoke haze and thermals, everyone silent with what they carry. Beat: exhalation after the climax; the miles finally feel like years.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the river town, the crew and surviving descendant families gather; the ledger's names are read aloud, Coral's birth name among them. Beat: public truth, private grief, communal grace.

chapters.title: Ministry Reckoning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Officials arrive to bury the story and find it already told; Wren's photographs and Reyes's copy make suppression pointless. Beat: the machinery of silence failing.

chapters.title: Ines's Answer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Her grandfather's final survey is published with the families' blessing; she asks Coral not to fly away from her. Beat: love offered without conditions for the first time.

chapters.title: Coral's Answer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He gives Wren the choice to stay or go—and she chooses them both, calling them family outright. Beat: found family named aloud; duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Last Flight of the Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He flies the chest's remaining contents to the families upriver, landing on a strip he cut himself twenty years ago and never told anyone about. Beat: coming home to a place he never admitted was home.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Wren's POV. The river runs low and honest; the town argues, grieves, and begins to build a memorial. Beat: aftermath with weight and lightness both.

chapters.title: The Bell Rung
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The outpost bell, recovered, is rung once for each name. Coral stands among the descendants instead of above them in the air. Beat: belonging, earned.

chapters.title: New Coordinates
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He and Ines chart the drowned outpost properly at last—on the map, in the record, in the open. Beat: the past given its true coordinates.

chapters.title: Compass and Horizon
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, closing. A year later: a new plane, Wren learning the controls, Ines beside him. He measures life in years now, and the horizon is a place they're going together, not away from. Beat: resolution—love, memory, and family all airborne.
